name: Curcumin
aliases: E100, E100(i), INS 100, INS 100(i), curcumin, curcumins, curcuma extract, turmeric extract, Curcuma longa, curcumina, curcumine, Kurkumin
what_is: Curcumin is the natural yellow pigment obtained from turmeric. In food it is used mainly as a colouring, and on a label it may appear as curcumin or E100.
why_botia: In a trial with 93 postmenopausal women, curcumin capsules reduced hot flushes over eight weeks compared with placebo. There were no statistically significant differences in anxiety, sexual function or overall symptoms. A food label does not establish a dose comparable with the capsules studied.
can_1: Detect E100, curcumin and curcuma or turmeric extract when they are declared on the label.
can_2: Explain what the clinical trial found and show the Woman and E-number information layers.
cannot_1: Determine how much curcumin a food contains, or whether it matches the dose used in the trial.
cannot_2: Tell anyone whether to take curcumin, or replace advice from a doctor.

sources.label: The effect of oral capsule of curcumin and vitamin E on the hot flashes and anxiety in postmenopausal women: A triple blind randomised controlled trial (2020)

title: Curcumin
description: Curcumin is the natural yellow pigment obtained from turmeric. In food it is used mainly as a colouring, and on a label it may appear as curcumin or E100.
robot_answers: Because being authorised as a colouring does not mean it can be used in any food or amount. E100 can be used only in the categories and under the conditions allowed by the applicable regulations.

Curcumin is one of the main pigments found in turmeric, but turmeric is the whole spice and contains many other compounds. E100 may be a curcumin preparation used specifically for colouring rather than the spice itself.
